deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the analysis-situs preliminaries, crosscuts (Querschnitte) of a surface T spread over the plane. It accompanies the material on conformal mapping and the Dirichlet minimum on the previous page. These are the ingredients of Riemann's 1851 dissertation (Grundlagen, Art. 5-6) and later of the 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen'. The boundary of T consists of closed curves, the Begrenzungsstücke; let b be their number.

Claim (line 1): every crosscut changes b by exactly +1 or -1.

A crosscut q is a simple arc running through the interior. It starts at a boundary point and ends either at a boundary point or at an earlier point of itself. After cutting, the new boundary consists of the old boundary plus both banks (q+, q-) of the cut. Riemann's first, struck-out case analysis begins 'a point of one boundary piece a with a point of another b'. The surviving text treats the self-terminating case. The full case split (my completion, consistent with the standard treatment):

(i) q joins component a to a different component b. Then a, q+, b and q- are traversed as a single closed curve, so b -> b-1.

(ii) q joins two points of the same component a. Then a is split into two arcs; each arc closes up with one bank of q into a closed curve, so b -> b+1.

(iii) Riemann's surviving case: q starts at a point of a and ends at an earlier point P of itself, giving a stem s from a to P and a loop l through P. After cutting:
- one bank of the loop l is a closed curve by itself. Riemann: 'das in sich zurücklaufende Stück desselben [bildet] einen Theil'.
- the other bank of l, plus both banks of the stem s, plus a, forms a second closed curve. Riemann: 'der Querschnitt nebst dem Begrenzungsstücke einen andern Theil'.
- each of these is 'ein in sich zurücklaufendes Begrenzungsstück'. So a is replaced by two components, b -> b+1.

Purpose: a crosscut lowers the order of connectivity by 1 (Euler characteristic chi -> chi+1). Combined with this lemma, the order of connectivity and the number of boundary pieces change parity together. This leads to Riemann's result that a closed surface made into a simply connected one by cuts has even connectivity number 2p (bounded surface: 2p+1-fach zusammenhängend). In modern terms, for an orientable compact surface with genus g and b boundary components, chi = 2-2g-b, and the cut changes b by ±1.
errors: The page itself only fully states case (iii), self-terminating crosscut. Cases (i) and (ii) appear only in struck-out drafts (case i begun, case ii absent). As a proof of the opening claim the page is therefore incomplete, though the claim is correct.

Implicit assumption: the surface is two-sided (orientable) and the crosscut is a simple arc. On a one-sided surface, case (ii) can leave b unchanged (e.g. a crosscut of a Möbius band from its boundary to itself can keep b=1). Riemann's surfaces spread over the plane are orientable, so no actual error.

results.what: Every crosscut of a (two-sided) bordered surface changes the number of boundary components by exactly ±1, with case analysis including a crosscut that ends at an earlier point of itself
results.modern_name: Effect of cutting along an arc on boundary components; parity relation between connectivity (first Betti number / Euler characteristic) and number of boundary curves
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann (Grundlagen 1851, Art. 6; Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen 1857, analysis-situs Lehrsätze)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known analysis-situs lemma Riemann published in his dissertation and the 1857 Abelian functions paper. It shows working-out of the case analysis but contains nothing new.

checkable.asserts: Case (i): crosscut joining two different boundary components keeps genus, b->b-1, chi->chi+1
Case (ii)/(iii) on a non-separating cut: genus drops by 1, b->b+1, chi->chi+1 consistently
Planar (g=0) case: cutting disk-with-holes along a same-component arc increases b by 1 and chi by 1

Connectivity order N=1-chi=2g+b-1 for orientable surfaces: N-b=2g-1 is odd, so N and b always have opposite parity (the parity relation the lemma serves; for a closed surface cut by one boundary point, N=2g)

transcription_corrections: Line 1 'Durch jeden Querschnitt wird die Anzahl der Begrenzungsstücke entweder um 1 vermindert oder um 1 vermehrt' — confirmed by image.

In the surviving paragraph, '{+geht entweder+}' is an insertion written above the line over a struck word; the reading 'Ein Querschnitt geht entweder von einem Punkte eines Begrenzungsstücks aus zu ... in einem frühern Punkte des Querschnitts' is plausible. The 'zu' at line end belongs to a struck/abandoned continuation ('zu [einem Punkte ...]', i.e. the two-boundary-points case), replaced by '[-oder er endigt-]' / 'in einem frühern Punkte'.
'bildet das in sich zurücklaufende Stück desselben einen Theil' — the image reads 'bildete'/'bildet'; 'Theil' here means a part of the new boundary, not a piece of the surface.
